title: The caret sits where the words will, and the outline follows the pill as you type
goal: Two things go wrong while you are typing a caption on an arrow. Press Return and the caret drops to the left edge of the new line, then the first character you type jumps to the middle: the caret was never where the words were going to be. And while the bubble grows and shrinks around what you type, the layer's own outline stays the shape it was when you started, so the box on screen stops describing the thing you are editing. The caret should sit where the next character will land, and the outline should follow the bubble.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-12: "when im typing in a pill in the arrow tool, and press enter, the cursor goes to the left of the next line. i type a char and it's centered. Why isn't the cursor where it should be? I like centered, i just expected the cursor to be there. Also as i'm typing and changing the shape of the pill the layer outline doesn't change with the shape of the content. It stays fixed."

Two bugs, filed as one task because they are in the same function and a runner fixing either is already standing in the right place. Both causes found by READING and not yet reproduced in the app; reproduce first.

CAUSE OF THE CARET, and it explains both halves of what the user saw exactly. Sources/Photonz/CanvasTextEditing.swift, layoutCaptionEditor, around line 327:

    let lines = CaptionMetrics.committedText(editor.string).contains(where: \.isNewline)
    if lines { editor.alignment = .center ... } else { editor.alignment = .left ... }

The alignment is chosen from the COMMITTED text, and CaptionMetrics.committedText (Sources/PhotonzRender/CaptionMetrics.swift:23) runs the commit rule ArrowCaptionEntry.caption(from:), which trims the edges — its comment says so: "a stray space or a trailing Return cannot shrink the bubble on commit". So with "Hello" typed and Return pressed, the field holds "Hello\n" but the committed text is "Hello", which contains no newline, so the field is left aligned and the caret goes to the left edge. Type one character and the committed text becomes "Hello\nX", the branch flips to centred, and the character appears in the middle. That is precisely the reported sequence.

THE TRAP in fixing it. Do not simply force .center. The single line branch deliberately uses .left with the container set to the pill width and positions the ink with editor.textContainerInset, computed from CaptionMetrics.textInset (same function, around line 311, with a comment explaining that the pill centres the ink rather than the box). Centring on top of that inset would double apply and slide the words. The narrow correct change is that TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS are currently sharing one string: alignment and container width should follow the DRAFT (editor.string, newline included, even a trailing one), while every MEASUREMENT — pillSize, textSize, and what commits — must keep using committedText, because not shrinking the bubble on a bare Return is exactly why committedText exists. Keep that behaviour; it is in the acceptance list as a thing that must not regress.

CAUSE OF THE OUTLINE. The same function measures the live pill (`var pill = CaptionMetrics.pillSize(for: editor.string, in: caption)`) but uses it only for the editor's own frame; nothing is written back. The layer's on canvas bounds take the caption from Layer.measuredCaptionPillSize (Sources/Photonz/CaptionPillSizing.swift:19), which reads the STORED caption (`caption ?? ""`), and the stored caption does not change until commit. So the selection chrome keeps the pre edit pill. The bounds are asked for in several places — CanvasView.swift:1085, CanvasGroups.swift:37 (captionPillSizing), CanvasPointerCue.swift:58 and :95, EditorState.swift:2027 — so decide in ONE place how a live draft reaches them rather than patching each call site, and say which you chose in the audit.

Worth deciding deliberately and recording: the alternative to a live outline is hiding it while the field is open, which is what the canvas already does with handles during a drag (CanvasDisplay.swift:913 and :932 gate on !dragInFlight). The user asked for it to follow, so follow; but if following turns out to fight the chrome at some zoom, hiding is the honest fallback and not a failure.

This sits in the shipped arrow captions work (epic-uehjr1, all done), including 'the caption bubble you type in is the exact width of the one that lands' and 'an arrow caption can hold more than one line' — the multi line case was added and the caret was never part of it.

Captions are behind the next-arrow-captions flag; check Sources/Photonz/Releases/ and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: Reproduce both first and record them: type a word, press Return, and note where the caret sits and where the first character of the second line lands; separately, type into a caption and note the outline against the growing bubble
Press Return in a caption and the caret sits centred on the new line, in the spot the next character will actually occupy
Typing that character does not move it: where the caret was is where the letter lands

The bubble does not change size when Return is pressed on its own, which is the behaviour that exists today and must not regress: a trailing Return still commits nothing and still leaves the pill the size of its words
The same holds on the third line and beyond, and on a line that is longer than the one above it
While you type, the layer's selection outline follows the bubble as it grows and shrinks, rather than keeping the shape it had when the field opened
The outline and the bubble agree on their edges at every zoom, checked at one hundred percent and zoomed in, since the two are drawn by different code paths
Committing leaves the outline exactly where the live one was: no jump at the moment the field closes
Deleting back to a single line returns both the caret and the outline to the single-line behaviour
Tests cover the alignment decision and the live bounds, written before the change, including the bare trailing Return case
A playtest walk types a two line caption and checks the caret and the outline
Audit under queue/audits/ with captures of the caret after Return and the outline mid-type, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mock is not the authority here, the user's sentence is. Two things they said were separable: 'I like centered, i just expected the cursor to be there' is a caret bug, and 'the layer outline doesn't change with the shape of the content' is a chrome bug. A first-time user meets the caret bug on their second line of every caption, which is why it is worth the p1; they meet the outline bug only when they go BACK to re-word a caption, which turned out to matter (see below). Shortest version: change the one question that was being asked of the wrong string, and publish one rectangle from the one place that already computes it. Nothing else built.

Reproduced both in the probe before changing anything, with numbers rather than pictures, because neither shows in a screenshot: the caret blinks and the probe window is never active so it does not even draw, and the outline is a dashed line to eyeball against a bubble. Added a read-only probe (CanvasNSView.playtestCaptionGeometry) and a walk. Caret, before: draft "Hello" caret 61.1 in of a 79.5 wide bubble; press Return and it drops to 16.4 while the bubble stays 79.5; type X and the letter lands at 33.8-45.3, about 17 points right of where the caret had been. Exactly the reported sequence. Outline, before: re-edit a caption and replace it with "Ok" and the outline stays (399,254,581,92) while the bubble is (620,277,80,46).

Cause of the caret, confirmed: layoutCaptionEditor asked CaptionMetrics.committedText whether the draft has more than one line, and the commit rule trims a trailing Return, so "Hello\n" answered 'one line' and the field stayed left aligned. Fix: CaptionMetrics.draftIsMultiLine(editor.string) decides the LAYOUT (alignment and container width) while every MEASUREMENT keeps asking the committed text, so a bare Return still commits nothing and still leaves the pill the size of its words. Pinned by CaptionDraftLayoutTests.

Cause of the outline: the selection box comes from CanvasDisplay.inkBox, which measures the STORED caption, and the stored caption does not change until commit. Decided in ONE place as the task asked: layoutCaptionEditor already works out the bubble's document rect every keystroke (it has to, to place the field), so it publishes it as captionDraftPillRect and inkBox unions it with the arrow's own ink through a new pure Layer.drawnBounds(liveCaptionPill:) in PhotonzCore. The stored label is left OUT rather than added, or replacing a long caption with a short one would be outlined at both sizes at once. No call site was patched; every other caller of the measured pill is asking about a caption that has landed.

Verified after: caret centred 38.9 in of 79.5 on the new line and the X lands centred on 39.55; third line the same; bubble unchanged by a bare Return (620,277,80,46) either side; deleting back through the Return returns to left alignment. Outline follows: bubble (620,277,80,46) gives outline (620,277,360,46), bubble (204,277,496,46) gives (204,277,776,46), identical numbers at 100% and zoomed in, and the outline after Command Return is the same rect the live one was, so nothing jumps.

The walk is a TEST, not a photograph. Added an expectCaption step (aligned / caret / outline) to the script format, parsed in PhotonzCore with tests, and checked in the harness. Proved it bites: reverting the alignment fix fails the run at step 17 ('the draft is laid out left, not centred; the field holds "Hello\n"'), and reverting the outline fix fails at step 54 naming both rectangles and how far out the worst edge is (221.3 points).
Scripts/test.sh green (5717 tests). Walk families run: caption 12/12, arrow 17/17, outline 6/6, select 9/9. Asked for a full sweep because inkBox is the box every selection outline is drawn from.

Left alone on purpose, said in the audit: a brand new arrow's FIRST caption has no outline at all while you type it, because the selection box is Select-tool chrome and the Arrow tool is still in hand (CanvasDisplay 'guard tool == .select'). That is long-standing and is why only the re-edit shows the reported symptom. Filed as a follow-up instead of fixed: the caret on an empty new line is drawn short (14.5 against 23.8), which is an AppKit extra-line-fragment font question and not a position one.
